overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when the chair announced at the January 8, 2024 meeting that the superintendent's contract would not be renewed without that topic on the notice; the other allegations were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint 1: the Nov. 13 and Dec. 4, 2023 executive session notice topics and announcements on the superintendent's contract were insufficient because they did not say a final decision might be reached.
allegations.key_passage: The notices and announcements for these executive session discussions were sufficient where they clearly identified the executive session purpose the Committee relied on and where they identified the specific nonunion personnel that was the subject of the discussions.

allegations.summary: Complaint 1 (footnote): the committee allegedly had to announce in open session that a vote not to renew the superintendent's contract had failed.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the Open Meeting Law contains no such requirement.

allegations.summary: Complaint 2: the chair announced at the Jan. 8, 2024 meeting that the superintendent's contract would not be renewed, but that topic was not on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because Mayor Christenson, as chair, anticipated that he would discuss the nonrenewal of Superintendent Noriega-Murphy's contract during the January 8, 2024, meeting—a topic of substantial interest, on which the public body had reached a decision in executive session—the topic should have been included on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint 2 (footnote): the public was allegedly never allowed to participate in the renewal or nonrenewal decision.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent this was intended as an additional allegation, we decline to review it where, even if true, it would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Allegations raised for the first time in requests for further review, not in the original complaints, were not reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review allegations that were not first raised in a complaint filed with the public body.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future findings of similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future findings of similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
